global_organization_chain: Summary Sheet: A three-paragraph summary that names the inhomogeneous transition matrix, data economy claim, forecast horizon, and simulated-annealing decision. -> The introduction restates the two parts and the preliminary model defines the state system.
Introduction: A compact problem target and a two-stage roadmap with a forecast-to-decision handoff. -> Preliminary notation and assumptions operationalize native and non-native speaker states.
State and symbol definitions: An operational vocabulary for the homogeneous state vector and its later extensions. -> The assumptions constrain admissible transitions and double-counting choices.
General, additional, and office assumptions: A layered premise set for the preliminary, modified, and office-location models. -> The N=2 transition graph turns the preliminary premises into a matrix.
Preliminary transition analysis: A four-state N=2 transition graph and the structural interpretation of Equation (1). -> Eigenanalysis asks what long-run composition this homogeneous matrix implies.

Homogeneous transition and scaling: Equations (1)-(12), a 44-state homogeneous matrix, and a four-year projection procedure. -> Table 1 and the long-run eigenvector test whether the homogeneous construction is plausible.

Short-run check and long-run diagnostic: Figure 2, Table 1, Equation (13), and the conclusion that time-varying mechanisms are necessary. -> The Modified Model opening enumerates the exact missing processes.

Inhomogeneous learner-migrant model: Figure 3, Equations (14)-(17), and a four-block English-specific transition system. -> UN projections and learning assumptions instantiate the 26-language recurrence.

Demographic, language, migration, and GDP inputs: Initial vectors, time-indexed rates, distance categories, candidate cities, and 2017/2067 economic inputs. -> The modified recurrence produces trajectories and the rating model consumes terminal population and GDP.

Language trajectories, migration, and office outcomes: Figures 4-8, Tables 2 and office assignments, and score differences for 2017 and 2067. -> Strengths/weaknesses qualify the method and the memo compresses the decisions for the client.

Uniformity sensitivity: A modified learning-rate equation plus Figures 7 and 8 with a scenario-specific ranking effect. -> The office application uses the baseline forecast while retaining sensitivity as an applicability boundary.

Rating and simulated annealing: A score definition, 19 candidate cities, annealing parameters, and stable five/six-office solutions. -> The 2017 and 2067 result tables compare alternatives and inform the memo.

Five-versus-six office decision: Six offices are preferred in the scored baseline, while five remain a viable future option under a cost-compensation condition. -> The memo states the same branch in client-facing terms and adds relocation suggestions.

Strengths and Weaknesses: Four claimed strengths and four admitted weaknesses linked to future repair directions. -> The memo uses the strengths to communicate results but should retain the limitations as decision boundaries.

COO memo: A two-page memo with four forecast findings, three 2017 preference assignments, 2067 relocations, and a conditional five-office branch. -> References and appendices provide the source and numeric trace that the memo itself omits.
References and Appendices: References, Tables 3-8, and Figures 9-12. -> The appendix closes the evidence trace but leaves reproducibility gaps for data snapshots and code.

moves: input: [ABS Summary Sheet] Globalization, geographic language dispersion, and sparse support data create a projection-and-office decision problem.
rhetorical job: [ABS Summary Sheet] Open with business stakes, reject a population-only baseline, and preview the complete two-model route.
analytical job: [ABS Summary Sheet] Separate language states, add migration and learning mechanisms, project to 2067, and pass the forecast to office optimization.
output: [ABS Summary Sheet] A three-paragraph summary that names the inhomogeneous transition matrix, data economy claim, forecast horizon, and simulated-annealing decision.
handoff: [ABS Summary Sheet] The introduction restates the two parts and the preliminary model defines the state system.

main_argument_chains.claim: The paper treats language projection and office placement as one forecast-to-decision pipeline.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Every office recommendation must retain a trace to the language, GDP, transport, cost, and coverage inputs that produced it.

main_argument_chains.claim: The homogeneous preliminary model is deliberately scaled from two languages to twenty-two before its long-run failure motivates revision.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the preliminary model as a transparent diagnostic baseline, not as a validated fifty-year forecast.

main_argument_chains.claim: The inhomogeneous repair adds learners, migrants, demographic blocks, feedback, and an English-specific partition in response to named baseline defects.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Preserve the time-indexed block dependencies and resolve the apparent one-period feedback lag before implementation.

main_argument_chains.claim: Learning, migration, policy, economics, education, and language family are intended to connect population dynamics with geographic language distribution.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Calibrate and normalize source-target transitions before attributing geographic outcomes to these mechanisms.

main_argument_chains.claim: Uniformity sensitivity changes attraction strength to show how popularity feedback alters English and Mandarin trajectories.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Treat the three curves as local scenarios until calibrated ranges, joint uncertainty, and decision switches are tested.

main_argument_chains.claim: The application combines projected language demand, GDP, transport, setup proxy, and language load into constrained office assignments.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Normalize units, elicit stakeholder weights, enforce coverage exactly, and document the optimizer before acting on score differences.

main_argument_chains.claim: The memo changes the receiving form from technical derivation to conditional executive action while retaining forecast branches.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Keep every compressed memo claim linked to a model artifact and state uncertainty, infeasibility, and review triggers explicitly.

warnings.warning: Equation (1) is a non-conservative population operator over overlapping language identities, not a stochastic Markov transition matrix; prose also reverses the gamma flow order implied by its entries.
Equation (2) writes a divergent limit with k still on the right and omits the initial-vector scale and dominance conditions needed for an asymptotic eigenvector result.
Equation (5) visibly prints 0.005 in entry (2,4), contradicting alpha_24=0.05 in Equation (4).
The Equation (6) eigenpair satisfies neither the printed nor nominal matrix, and its vector sums to 3.248 despite being interpreted as population proportions.
Figure 2's threshold uses an ordinate labeled proportion that rises above one, so the plotted quantity is likely an unnormalized eigenvector component.
Equation (10) uses gamma_(i,N+j), transposing the target-row/source-column convention used by Equations (1), (7), (11), and (12).
Equation (11)'s 22 printed normalized values sum to 1.0387; the raw values sum to 1239.7 and appear divided by the mistyped denominator 1193.7.
Equation (12) allocates Gamma_i using shares normalized over all j while the preceding rule excludes j=i, so the retained rates do not sum to Gamma_i.
Equation (13) omits the full 44-vector and operator, preventing independent verification of the reported 0.9601 Punjabi component and eigenvalue.
Equations (14)-(15) update A^(n+1) from Y^(n) while advancing with A^(n), creating a one-period lag unless that timing is explicitly intended.
Equation (16) gives only proportional initial non-native English components and no total or normalization, so the starting vector is underidentified.

Equation (17) depends on an eagerness normalization that is not supplied; d is called similarity although larger values mean greater difficulty, and most time-indexed factors are fixed immediately afterward.
The sensitivity formula is paired with a low-uniformity subsection whose first sentence says high uniformity; the prose also types 0:1 while the figure shows k=0.1.
h_i is described as rent or setup cost but Equation (18b) derives it only from local GDP, transport cost, and the constant 10.
The cooling recurrence is only implied by alpha; the source omits the actual schedule, temperature-step count, and stopping trace.
The assignment objective and MEC domain must be reconstructed from prose, while the 2067 six-office result itself violates mutual exclusivity by assigning French twice.
